title: Bar Yochana
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman says Bar Yochana was from the Land of Israel and lived in Rome. He places the story during a stay in Rome by Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. [Bar Yochana] wished to give a feast for Rome’s leading men and consulted his fellow townsman, as related in Esther Rabbah 2:4.

notes.text: The consulted Esther Rabbah paragraph makes Bar Yochani the feast-giver who consults Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Yose. The supplied notice’s pronouns are compressed; the bracket identifies that reading. Its heading spells Yochana, and its abbreviated ר״א does not spell out Elazar/Eliezer. No canonical name change is made.

The saved whole Torat Emet EstherRabbah2:4 scalar explicitly makes Bar Yochani the feast-giver consulting Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Yose. This supports the bracketed subject and Eliezer expansion, superseding the old Elazar alternative. Source heading Yochana and named Yochani remain different. Hyman owns the native-origin and Shimon-bar-Yochai travel context; the matched episode does not newly prove that joint journey. כדמבוא is contextually as related, not an identified introduction. No filial or authority identity is admitted.

Esther Rabbah 2:4 calls the feast-giver Bar Yochani and identifies his townsman as Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Yose. Hyman’s print (vol. I, p. 286) has the heading Bar Yochana and the abbreviated ר״א, and reads כדמובא (“as related”), beside the supplied כדמבוא. The separate Roman mission in Meilah 17b names Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yose alongside Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. That account leaves the spelling in the feast story intact.
